outline.chapter_title: From Cameo Videos to the Second Circuit
outline.description: This chapter introduces the dispute, the parties, and the factual sequence that produced the lawsuit. It explains how Jimmy Kimmel obtained personalized Cameo videos from George Santos under fictitious names, repurposed them for the recurring television segment 'Will Santos Say It?," and how Santos responded with federal copyright and related state law claims. It also situates the appeal by describing the district court’s Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal and the issues presented to the Second Circuit.

outline.chapter_title: Appellate Posture and the Pleading-Stage Fair Use Inquiry
outline.description: This chapter explains the procedural lens through which the Second Circuit reviewed the case. It covers de novo review of a Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal, the materials an appellate court may consider at that stage, and why fair use—although an affirmative defense—can sometimes be resolved on the face of the complaint without discovery.

outline.chapter_title: The Fair Use Framework and the Court’s Focus on Transformative Purpose
outline.description: This chapter lays out the governing fair use doctrine and then centers on the first statutory factor, which drove the court’s analysis. It shows how the panel framed the key question as whether Kimmel’s use had a different purpose and character from Santos’s original videos, and why Santos’s arguments about authorship, intent, and bad faith did not defeat fair use.

The conclusion that the first factor strongly favored fair use

outline.chapter_title: The Remaining Fair Use Factors and Why Copyright Claims Failed as a Matter of Law
outline.description: This chapter explains how the court addressed the other fair use factors and why none saved Santos’s copyright claims. It emphasizes the court’s treatment of publication status, market harm, and the difference between reputational or critical injury and cognizable copyright market usurpation. It also shows why the overall balance permitted affirmance at the pleading stage.

outline.chapter_title: State Law Claims, Unresolved Preemption, and the Final Affirmance
outline.description: This chapter covers the non-copyright claims and the court’s choice to affirm on state-law pleading grounds without deciding copyright preemption. It analyzes the direct contract claim under the Cameo Terms of Service, the implied contract theory, and the fraudulent inducement claim, then closes with the case’s practical significance for pleading around copyright and for media uses of commissioned content.
